summary: Through the Space: Mission Mars is a free Roblox game where kids aged 7 to 12 run a Martian outpost and feel the real engineering trade-offs of a mission. Every trip outside balances three resources (life support/oxygen, power and radiation dose) that follow real NASA data, like Curiosity's 0.67 mSv per day and NASA's 600 mSv career limit, so no choice is free. Dust storms stop solar charging, dust covers the suit's solar panel (like NASA's InSight lander), the ship and deep mine shield radiation, a greenhouse produces oxygen, and every message to Earth takes 3 to 22 minutes, just like the real light delay. A friend can play Mission Control on Earth and sees the crew's data minutes late. Every number shows its NASA source in the game, missions change every playthrough, and a minute-by-minute mission chart plus the same quiz before and after the mission show what the player learned. It matters because kids usually see only the outcome of a space mission, not the decisions behind it; here they make those decisions themselves, in English or Spanish, with a read-aloud voice for young readers. Two ways to play: in any web browser with no download or account (https://prosito0284.github.io/proyecto-nasa/) or as the full 3D game on Roblox (https://www.roblox.com/games/126948880861294).
details: TWO WAYS TO PLAY - Web version (no download, no account): https://prosito0284.github.io/proyecto-nasa/ - Full 3D Roblox version (PC, tablet, phone): https://www.roblox.com/games/126948880861294 WHAT IT DOES Through the Space: Mission Mars is a Roblox game for kids aged 7-12. Players live in a Mars ship-outpost: they build the RMA-01 robot, put on a suit, go outside to collect samples on a glacier, analyze the air (250 CO2, 7 N2, 5 Ar, 1 other = Mars' real air), mine minerals, make water, oxygen and rocket fuel with real chemistry (like the Sabatier reactor on the ISS), grow a greenhouse and fly to Deimos. HOW IT ANSWERS THE CHALLENGE - Three core resources only: life support (O2), power and radiation dose. O2 drops outside (faster if you run); power is spent by the drone and recharged by a solar panel; radiation adds up and never goes down. - No free choice: exploring longer gives more samples but more radiation and less oxygen; the drone costs power; glacier ice runs out; the flight back from Deimos costs fuel; the greenhouse costs water. - Radiation shielding: the ship and the deep mine shield you; in the mine the RAD bar shows "SHIELDED" and explains why. - Power: dust storms stop solar charging (2018 global dust storm) and dust slowly covers the suit's solar panel (like NASA's InSight) until a dust devil passes close and cleans it (like Spirit and Opportunity). A dust wall appears on the horizon before each storm, so kids can decide to go back. - Food production: the greenhouse grows plants that make oxygen tubes. - Communication delay: the ship's radio talks to Earth with the real light-time delay (3 to 22.4 minutes one way, compressed in game time). Earth's warnings arrive late. In multiplayer, a friend can play Mission Control on Earth and sees the crew's O2, power and radiation as they were minutes ago; their messages arrive late too. Playing alone, the radio shows "what Earth sees" about you. - Replayability: samples move every game, dust storms and solar storms (based on the real September 2017 event) come at random times; a failure screen explains the real science and lets you retry from a checkpoint. HOW IT HELPS KIDS LEARN - A "Before you go out" screen next to the door shows the player's O2, power, radiation, panel dust, weather and Earth's light-minutes, like a real pre-EVA check. - At the end, a mission report compares their dose with Earth and NASA's limit, and a minute-by-minute chart shows O2, power and radiation with every trip outside and every event. - Learning is measured: the same 4 questions (air, radiation, gravity, communication delay) are asked before and after the mission; the report shows "before -> now" and the game keeps anonymous totals. - A 6-stop "5-minute tour" for judges and classrooms, each stop with its real NASA number and source. - Accessibility: English and Spanish, big-text mode, a read-aloud voice (Roblox text-to-speech), alerts with sound and text, bars with numbers and icons. Works on PC, tablet and phone. REAL DATA AND HONESTY 20 NASA data points, each with its source on screen ("NASA data used" button). Static data is never shown as live; Curiosity's current sol is fetched live from mars.nasa.gov and labeled LIVE only when it loads. Game assumptions (compressed time, game shielding values, raised Deimos gravity) are stated in the game. TOOLS Roblox Studio, Luau, Roblox DataStores and MemoryStore, HttpService, Roblox AudioTextToSpeech. AI assistants (Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini) helped write and test code and documents; ground/rock/ice textures were made with Roblox Studio's AI material generator (decoration, not data). The team designed the game, chose and checked the NASA data and made all decisions.
